paths.description: Homepage and primary news discovery template; tested desktop/mobile, preferences, navigation, performance, privacy and memory.
International section listing representing category/index templates.
Live article representing editorial detail/live-blog pages and rich metadata.
Live TV page representing media playback and channel-selection surfaces.
Newsletter selection and email submission representing the primary form journey.
Nonexistent route representing HTTP/network recovery state.

findings.summary: Throttled mobile loading misses the good LCP range by a wide margin.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 17.7 s, FCP 3.7 s, Speed Index 6.7 s, and a performance score of 0.61. The unthrottled trace was much faster (LCP 1.36 s), showing strong sensitivity to constrained conditions.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP element and its request chain, prioritise its discovery, defer non-critical advertising/player work, and verify under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: The homepage loads an excessive dependency and media payload with render-blocking resources.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 255 requests and 14,026,061 transferred bytes, including about 9.94 MB of live-stream XHR. Lighthouse estimates 2,230 ms render-blocking savings and 301 KiB cache-lifetime savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not fetch live video segments before user intent, shorten the critical chain, defer non-critical scripts/styles, and set effective cache lifetimes.

findings.summary: Numerous text and UI combinations fail minimum colour contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s color-contrast audit failed with 40 affected elements and the high-contrast emulation produced an unchanged capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to WCAG AA and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast treatment for essential controls and text.

findings.summary: Security policy headers and cookie flags are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The header audit found no Content-Security-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Three first-party cookies are not Secure, and several are SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive nonce/hash-based CSP, a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and mark HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest workable SameSite policy.

findings.summary: The homepage has a broad tracking and third-party collection footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe observed 21 third-party origins and a known Google advertising tracker; the HAR recorded 188 third-party requests and 12.16 MB third-party transfer. Multiple analytics identifiers persist for 395 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit and remove non-essential vendors, delay optional analytics/ads until valid consent, shorten identifier lifetimes, and batch/minimise events.

findings.summary: Live media and third-party work consume a disproportionate homepage budget before explicit user intent.
findings.evidence: About 9.94 MB of live-stream segments were fetched during an 8-second homepage capture; total transfer reached 14.03 MB and third parties accounted for 12.16 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace automatic stream startup with a poster and explicit play action, then defer player, ad, and analytics dependencies until needed.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The light and dark 360×800 captures are byte-for-byte identical (189,184 bytes), and the dark-mode probe still computes the body background as rgb(255,255,255).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and retint surfaces, text, controls, and embedded UI with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), preserving brand contrast.

findings.summary: A large empty advertising/loading region pushes primary content below the first desktop viewport.
findings.evidence: The 1440×1000 capture shows roughly 300 px of blank space below the navigation before the lead story begins, reducing first-view content density.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse unfilled ad slots, reserve only the final creative size when an ad is confirmed, and prioritise editorial content in the first viewport.

findings.summary: The newsletter form’s invalid state is not announced or connected to a recovery message.
findings.evidence: Submitting the selected newsletter with an empty email leaves aria-invalid and aria-describedby unset, creates no aria-live/role=alert region, and does not move focus to the invalid field.
findings.suggestedFix: On attempted submission, set aria-invalid, attach a specific error with aria-describedby, announce it in a live region, and focus the first invalid field.

findings.summary: Substantial unused JavaScript and CSS are delivered on the homepage.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 656 KiB unused JavaScript and 58 KiB unused CSS, plus 17 KiB avoidable legacy JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Split page-specific bundles, conditionally load player/ad dependencies, remove duplicate/legacy code, and ship only CSS needed by the current template.

findings.summary: The newsletter email field has no accessible label.
findings.evidence: After selecting a newsletter, the email input has label count 0, no aria-label, and only placeholder="Votre email".
findings.suggestedFix: Add a persistent visible <label for> for the email input; keep placeholder text supplemental rather than using it as the name.

findings.summary: Heading hierarchy and menu expanded-state semantics are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The homepage contains an empty H1 and Lighthouse reports a heading-order failure. Opening the mobile menu changes the visual state but aria-expanded remains false and aria-controls is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a meaningful H1, keep heading levels sequential, and synchronise aria-expanded/aria-controls with the menu panel and focus lifecycle.

findings.evidence: The image primitive found 8 images without dimensions; Lighthouse’s unsized-images audit lists 14 affected image elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height attributes or a stable aspect-ratio for every content image to reserve layout space.

findings.summary: The page uses a deprecated API and omits source maps for large first-party scripts.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports one deprecation warning and three large first-party scripts without valid source maps.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the deprecated API usage and publish production source maps to support debugging and platform hygiene.

findings.summary: Some navigation links are not crawlable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 12 anchors without crawlable destinations, despite the viewport and robots configuration otherwise being present.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href URLs for navigation and reserve buttons for in-page actions; retain descriptive link text.

findings.summary: Image delivery leaves meaningful byte and rendering savings.
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 55 use legacy formats, 37 lack srcset, 36 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded, and 11 are oversized; Lighthouse estimates 479 KiB image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP sources, size them to rendered slots, lazy-load below-fold images, and retain explicit dimensions.

findings.summary: Navigation and menu state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition CSS; the menu interaction video and getAnimations() probe show an immediate state swap with no active animation.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance menu and same-site navigation with same-document or cross-document View Transitions, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: The newsletter email field does not advertise its autofill purpose.
findings.evidence: The rendered input is type=email but autocomplete is empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete="email" and preserve appropriate inputmode/type semantics.
